title: Entitlement mesh, decision cache, and SSO claim mapper for unified authorization
creator: Aisha Grant
description: Problem: Our current authorization checks are fragmented across API gateways, runtime interceptors, and the admin console. This leads to inconsistent enforcement, duplicated policy evaluation work, and noisy audit logs. SSO/SAML assertions are mapped inconsistently into claims which makes attribute-based checks brittle. Goal: build an 'entitlement mesh' — a small, horizontally scalable service that centralizes policy decision results, provides a fast in-memory decision cache with invalidation hooks, and a claim-mapping adapter that normalizes SAML/SSO assertions into canonical RBAC attributes for the rest of the stack. The service will be the canonical source for allow/deny decisions at request time and a low-latency sidecar or library will integrate with API/runtime/console paths. It must support multi-tenant isolation, policy version pinning, and audit enrichment for downstream sinks.
acceptance_criteria: Decision mesh service deployed behind internal load balancer and reachable by API/runtime/console components
Decision cache returns cached allow/deny within 5ms p50 for repeat decisions; miss path falls back to policy evaluator and populates cache
Cache invalidation event triggers within 2s of policy publish/update for affected tenants
SSO/SAML claim mapper normalizes at least: email, groups, roles, tenant_id, and federation_id across IdP variants
Audit events include decision_id, policy_version, input_snapshot (hash), and upstream correlation_id and are delivered to the audit stream
A/B rollout: runtime components can toggle between local evaluation and mesh-based decisions per route
Security review completed and penetration test checklist items resolved
notes: Design choices considered: 1) full remote PDP for every call (simple but high latency); 2) hybrid cache + remote PDP (chosen for latency/cost balance); 3) compile policies to eBPF/WASM and run locally (future exploration).

Cache key format: tenant|policy_hash|principal_claims_hash|resource_fingerprint. TTL default 60s with configurable per-policy hints. Policy publish events will carry invalidation lists (tenant-scoped keys) to avoid broad flushes.

Claim normalizer will be implemented as a small library used by the SAML assertion processor and offered as an optional sidecar for legacy consumers. Mapping rules will be declarative and storeable in the policy catalog so customers can adjust mapping for custom IdPs.

We will expose traces and a decision-level metric (decisions/sec, cache_hit_rate, avg_latency) in Console. Rollback plan: flip runtime config back to local evaluator + degrade to allowlist for low-risk routes.
Privacy: input_snapshot stored as a SHA256 hash in audit events; raw attributes only kept in short-term logs with strict retention and access controls.
